solutions.explanation:
The two factors in each denominator differ by \(2\), so a difference of reciprocals produces the desired numerator:
\[
\frac1{(2k-1)(2k+1)}
=\frac12\left(\frac1{2k-1}-\frac1{2k+1}\right).
\]
Here \(k\) runs from \(1\) through \(128\), because \(2(128)-1=255\). All denominators are positive.

Writing the sum in this form reveals the cancellation:
\[
\begin{aligned}
S=\frac12\bigg[&\left(1-\frac13\right)
+\left(\frac13-\frac15\right)+\cdots\\
&+\left(\frac1{255}-\frac1{257}\right)\bigg].
\end{aligned}
\]
Every reciprocal from \(1/3\) through \(1/255\) occurs once positively and once negatively. Only the endpoints remain, so
\[
S=\frac12\left(1-\frac1{257}\right)
=\boxed{\frac{128}{257}}.
\]
The answer is \(\boxed{\text{D}}\).
solutions.title: Cancel consecutive reciprocal terms
